**Holding.** No. Action with the effect of law must pass both houses and be presented to the President. One-house and two-house legislative vetoes are unconstitutional.

**Question.** Whether one house of Congress could, by resolution, override an executive decision to suspend an individual's deportation, as the immigration statute then allowed.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the opinion** (official text)

[Opinion: 462 U.S. 919](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USREPORTS-462/pdf/USREPORTS-462-919.pdf){.btn-official}
:::

Background reading: [Wikipedia article on INS v. Chadha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_and_Naturalization_Service_v._Chadha) (secondary source).

## Why it matters

Chadha invalidated the legislative veto device built into many national security statutes of the 1970s. It cast doubt on the [War Powers Resolution](../statutes/wpr-1973.qmd) provision letting Congress order a withdrawal by concurrent resolution and on the original concurrent-resolution procedures of the [National Emergencies Act](../statutes/nea-1976.qmd) and the [Arms Export Control Act](../statutes/aeca-1976.qmd), and it is why most congressional checks in this wiki now take the form of joint resolutions, which the President can veto.

## How Congress responded

Congress replaced the vetoes with joint resolutions: expedited joint resolution procedures for the War Powers Resolution (1983), joint resolutions to terminate national emergencies (1985), and joint resolutions of disapproval for arms sales (1986).

## Status

Good law.

## Statutes at issue

- [War Powers Resolution](../statutes/wpr-1973.qmd){.subj}. Undercut Sec. 5(c), which provides for withdrawal of forces by concurrent resolution.
- [National Emergencies Act](../statutes/nea-1976.qmd){.subj}. Undercut termination of emergencies by concurrent resolution; Congress substituted a joint resolution in 1985.
- [Arms Export Control Act](../statutes/aeca-1976.qmd){.subj}. Undercut the concurrent resolution of disapproval for arms sales; Congress substituted a joint resolution in 1986.

Studied in [Unit 1: Where the power comes from](../study/units/foundations.qmd).
